prize_parts.citation: For developing methods to estimate demand and market power in differentiated-product industries with endogenous prices and heterogeneous consumers.

statement.case_for: My preferred part is unchanged: the demand-estimation core of B024 (Berry 1994; Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes 1995). Having read the exchange, I tested it against the criteria that colleagues on both the B040 and B044 sides use: conceptual or empirical advance, influence in practice, durability, and clarity of attribution. BLP made it possible to estimate substitution patterns, markups and welfare from market data when prices are endogenous and consumers are heterogeneous. That changed what researchers and regulators can know, and the tools are routine in merger review, antitrust, trade, health and environmental economics. The papers are about thirty years old and have been extended and criticised heavily, so the record is mature. The credit can be limited to a three-person core that matches the originating papers, with the citation confined to demand estimation. Hassler argues that influence on quantitative models and policy analysis is the right test of durability for a foundational mechanism. I accept that test, and I think the BLP framework meets it at least as well as the alternatives. I do not want to overstate this. The configuration has a single explicit supporter and no path to six votes at present, and I am not treating that as evidence for or against its merit.
statement.case_against: The main reservation is that this is chiefly a methodological contribution, and a committee that wants a discovery in the narrow sense may weigh it lower. Structural demand estimates depend on functional-form and instrument assumptions, so credibility varies by application. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin, and the wider structural-IO programme, lie outside a three-name award. That boundary is a defensible but real cut. Several members describe B040 as having the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, which is a more compact claim than mine. After this round I think that comparison is fair. Where B024 and B040 are close on maturity and influence, B040 has the cleaner two-person credit. My remaining argument for B024 is that a mechanism's simplicity should not decide the matter when the empirical framework has changed practice just as much. I am also aware that my own field is close to B024, which could inflate my weighting of its practical impact.

responses.point: Hassler holds that B040's attribution is cleanest and that influence on quantitative models and policy analysis is the better test of durability than direct empirical identification. In round 1 he ranked B024 sixth, saying Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are peripheral to the core method, and he asked how much weight methodological contributions should carry.
responses.response: I accept his test of influence on quantitative practice and apply it to BLP, where it points the same way. I also agree with his view that the extra names are peripheral to the core method, which is why my part keeps three names and a citation limited to demand estimation. Two points remain between us. First, if mixed empirical validation is a weakness common to foundational mechanisms but not disqualifying, as he says of B040, then functional-form sensitivity of structural estimates should be treated the same way. Second, I accept that B040's two-person credit is tighter than my three-person credit. I count that as a real advantage and it is why B040 is now my first alternative. It does not change my view of the relative size of the two contributions.

responses.point: Andersson prefers B040 because the originating contribution sits with two people. The attribution property is the one valued most, and the three-name limit forces arbitrary choices for candidates like B024. Andersson also lists B024 as an alternative and cites the overlap with the 2022 prize as the main risk to B040.
responses.response: The point about forced cuts applies to B024 as the full seven-name credited set, and I agree. The BLP core is the part I would credit, and the originating papers are by Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, so the cap does not force an arbitrary choice inside that core. The separate empirical entry and dynamic-model strands are left out, and I would say so openly. I agree that clean attribution is a legitimate criterion and I weigh it heavily, which is why B040 is my main alternative. I would not rank it above B024 on that criterion alone. On overlap, I found the colleagues who distinguish collateral-constraint amplification from bank-run and crisis work more persuasive than the narrowing argument, so I am not marking down B040 for it.

responses.point: Krusell now prefers B044 with Autor, Dorn and Hanson. He anchors the citation on trade-shock evidence, where attribution is clean and over a decade of replication has refined the effect sizes. He treats the attribution of B040 as the cleanest but sees its empirical test as more indirect.
responses.response: I agree that the trade-shock attribution is clean and that a decade of scrutiny is a fair test, and I ranked B044 fifth for attribution and strength of evidence, not for lack of merit. My point concerns consistency. B044 is essentially a credibly identified research design plus findings, and the committee is rightly weighing it against concerns about shift-share inference. If the committee accepts a design-based empirical contribution as prize-worthy, it should not discount B024 simply for being methodological. The two differ in maturity: BLP has about thirty years behind it and the trade-shock papers about ten. That is where I rank them differently, and I record B044's shorter record as the reason.

responses.point: Boppart prefers B036 with Helpman and Melitz, argues that firm heterogeneity is distinct from the trade theory recognised in 2008, and lists the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as the strongest reservation. Boppart ranked B024 last of eight, citing the large credited group and its partly methodological character.
responses.response: I agree with the distinction from the 2008 recognition, and I ranked B036 second. The omission of co-originators weighs on B036 and on B024. The difference is in how the cut falls. For B036, the missing firm-level evidence is the part the model rationalised, and for B024 it is outside the core. I think the BLP three-person core is more identifiable than the size of the credited set suggests, as I argued in round 1. I would not treat the large listed set as a reason to dismiss the candidate. I also keep to my round-1 position that the absence of a dedicated trade prize since 2008 is not a scientific merit argument for B036.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will weight a methodological advance on a par with a conceptual mechanism (B040) or a credibly identified empirical design (B044), and whether it wants that kind of prize this year.
How the committee should treat the omission of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin under a three-name limit, and whether limiting credit to demand estimation is clear enough.
How sensitive structural demand estimates are to functional-form and instrument assumptions. I rely on general knowledge and the openings and have not verified this independently.
How much the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises reduces the case for B040. The colleagues' descriptions are their own knowledge and have not been verified here.

Whether B040's cleaner attribution should outweigh B024 on the common criteria, and whether my field proximity to B024 biases my weighting. I have not settled this, and B040 is the alternative I would most readily support.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn or any other credited name on the shortlist is apparent from my supplied profile. I disclose that my research is in industrial organization and international trade, close to B024 and B036, and I have tried to apply the common criteria. I have co-authored with committee chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen (IJIO 2026), and the chair supports B040, one of my alternatives. Neither of them is a credited candidate, and I do not adjudicate these ties. My spouse's public political role is noted only as a public fact, with no apparent bearing on these ballots.
